correctness.rationale: From folded Skellam masses p0=e^(−a−b)I0(z), pk=2e^(−a−b)cosh(kθ)I_k(z), z=2sqrt(ab), θ=(log a/b)/2, k≥1, the k≥2 log-curvature sign compares Rk=I_k²/(I_(k−1)I_(k+1)) and Qk=1+sinh²θ/cosh²(kθ). Classical strict Bessel Turán gives k1 positive even after special factor two at zero. Writing I_k=(z/2)^k A_k(ab)/k! and using positivity yields Rk≥(k+1)²/[k(k+1)+ab]; for ab≤1 this exceeds Qk<1+1/k². For any fixed k≥2, I_k(z)/I0(z)→1 as z→∞ so Rk→1<Qk for fixed θ≠0: choose s large simultaneously for finite k=2..K. For each fixed ab and θ, lower bound Rk−1=Ω(1/k), while Qk−1=O(e^(−2k|θ|)), proving eventual strict logconcavity. Rational Bessel series at a=3,b=12 has p2²<p1p3. Numerically independent high-z k2..7 checks corroborate but the analytic limiting comparison proves infinite statement.
residual_risks: ab≤1 is sufficient, not a claimed sharp boundary; high-intensity logconvex block can be low mass.
Fixed K first, then s large: there is no claim that one fixed distribution has infinitely many logconvex indices; every fixed pair eventually becomes logconcave.
